title: Invariants of a tensor product with a field extension under a group with fixed field the base
statement: Let $k\subseteq M$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] and $G$ a group of $k$-algebra automorphisms of $M$ whose fixed field is $k$: $\{y\in M:\tau(y)=y\text{ for all }\tau\in G\}=k$. Let $A$ be a $k$-vector space, and for $\tau\in G$ let $\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\tau:A\otimes_kM\to A\otimes_kM$ be the $k$-linear map with $a\otimes y\mapsto a\otimes\tau(y)$. Then the $k$-linear map $\iota:A\to A\otimes_kM$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, is injective, and its image is exactly the set of invariants $\{z\in A\otimes_kM:(\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\tau)(z)=z\text{ for all }\tau\in G\}$. (In particular, for a $k$-algebra $A$, $(A\otimes_kM)^G=A\otimes1\cong A$.)

source.place: Varieties, proof of Lemma 038B (lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois), lines 924-925: '$(A\otimes_kk')^G[T]=A[T]$ (by basic Galois theory)'; the argument (choose a $k$-basis $(e_i)$ of $A$, so $A\otimes_kM=\bigoplus_ie_i\otimes M$ and $\mathrm{id}\otimes\tau$ acts coordinatewise) is not written in the source

proof.text: A basis of $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector] (with $K=k$, $V=A$, $S=\emptyset$) the $k$-vector space $A$ has a $k$-basis $(e_i)_{i\in I}$: every $a\in A$ is $a=\sum_{i\in I}c_ie_i$ for a unique family $(c_i)_{i\in I}$ of elements of $k$, almost all zero.

source.place: Varieties, proof of Lemma 038B (lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois), lines 924-925: '$(A\otimes_kk')^G[T]=A[T]$ (by basic Galois theory)'; the argument is not written in the source and is written out by the agent

proof.text: Coordinates in $A\otimes_kM$. By [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension] (with $K=k$, $L=M$, $V=A$), $A\otimes_kM$ is an $M$-vector space with $\lambda\cdot(a\otimes\mu)=a\otimes\lambda\mu$, and since $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ is a $k$-basis of $A$ (step 1), $(e_i\otimes1)_{i\in I}$ is an $M$-basis of $A\otimes_kM$. Hence every $z\in A\otimes_kM$ can be written as $z=\sum_iy_i\cdot(e_i\otimes1)=\sum_ie_i\otimes y_i$ for a unique family $(y_i)_{i\in I}$ of elements of $M$, almost all zero $(*)$.

source.place: Varieties, proof of Lemma 038B (lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois), lines 924-925: '$(A\otimes_kk')^G[T]=A[T]$ (by basic Galois theory)'; the argument is not written in the source and is written out by the agent

proof.text: $\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\tau$ acts coordinatewise. Let $\tau\in G$. The map $\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\tau$ exists by the universal property of $A\otimes_kM$ [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension], applied to the $k$-bilinear map $(a,y)\mapsto a\otimes\tau(y)$ ($\tau$ is $k$-linear, being a $k$-algebra map). It is additive and sends $e_i\otimes y$ to $e_i\otimes\tau(y)$, so for $z=\sum_ie_i\otimes y_i$ as in $(*)$, $(\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\tau)(z)=\sum_ie_i\otimes\tau(y_i)$, where $(\tau(y_i))_i$ is again almost all zero ($\tau(0)=0$); so this is the expression $(*)$ of $(\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\tau)(z)$.

source.place: Varieties, proof of Lemma 038B (lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois), lines 924-925: '$(A\otimes_kk')^G[T]=A[T]$ (by basic Galois theory)'; the argument is not written in the source and is written out by the agent

proof.text: The image of $\iota$ consists of invariants. $\iota$ is $k$-linear since $\otimes$ is $k$-bilinear. For $a\in A$ and $\tau\in G$, $(\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\tau)(a\otimes1)=a\otimes\tau(1)=a\otimes1$, as $\tau$ is a ring homomorphism. So $\iota(A)\subseteq(A\otimes_kM)^G$.

source.place: Varieties, proof of Lemma 038B (lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois), lines 924-925: '$(A\otimes_kk')^G[T]=A[T]$ (by basic Galois theory)'; the argument is not written in the source and is written out by the agent

proof.text: Every invariant lies in the image of $\iota$. Let $z\in A\otimes_kM$ with $(\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\tau)(z)=z$ for all $\tau\in G$, and write $z=\sum_ie_i\otimes y_i$ as in $(*)$. By step 3, $\sum_ie_i\otimes\tau(y_i)=\sum_ie_i\otimes y_i$, so by the uniqueness in $(*)$ (step 2) $\tau(y_i)=y_i$ for every $i\in I$ and every $\tau\in G$. By the hypothesis that the fixed field of $G$ is $k$, each $y_i$ lies in $k$ [def-pc-field-extension]: $y_i=c_i\cdot1$ with $c_i\in k$, and $c_i=0$ whenever $y_i=0$ (the map $k\to M$ is injective), so $(c_i)_i$ is almost all zero. By $k$-bilinearity of $\otimes$, $z=\sum_ie_i\otimes c_i1=\sum_i(c_ie_i)\otimes1=\iota\big(\sum_ic_ie_i\big)$. With step 4, the image of $\iota$ is exactly $(A\otimes_kM)^G$.

source.place: Varieties, proof of Lemma 038B (lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois), lines 924-925: '$(A\otimes_kk')^G[T]=A[T]$ (by basic Galois theory)'; the argument is not written in the source and is written out by the agent

proof.text: $\iota$ is injective. Let $a\in A$ with $\iota(a)=0$ and write $a=\sum_ic_ie_i$ (step 1). Then $0=\iota(a)=\sum_ie_i\otimes c_i1$, and $0=\sum_ie_i\otimes0$ is also an expression as in $(*)$, so by its uniqueness (step 2) $c_i1=0$ in $M$ for every $i$. The ring homomorphism $k\to M$ is injective [def-pc-field-extension], so $c_i=0$ for all $i$ and $a=0$. The parenthetical clause: for a $k$-algebra $A$, $\iota$ is then a bijection of $A$ onto $(A\otimes_kM)^G=\iota(A)=A\otimes1$.
